description: Figure 5(b) illustrates the ratio of training loss for several methods relative to the Vanilla baseline as a function of compute, with multiple colored line series overlaid. The x-axis is labeled “FLOPs” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning approximately from \(10^{17}\) to \(10^{19}\) with major ticks at \(10^{17}\), \(10^{18}\), and \(10^{19}\). The y-axis is labeled “Loss Ratio” on a linear scale, ranging from about 0.8 to 1.4 with regularly spaced tick labels at 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, and 1.4. A horizontal gray reference line at 1.0 indicates parity with Vanilla. The plotted series are solid lines without visible markers: the blue “Vanilla” line is flat at 1.0 across the full FLOPs range; the orange “StrmLLM (n=64)” line starts near about 1.25 at the left edge and decreases toward roughly 1.05 by the right edge; the green “SepLLM (n=64)” line begins around about 1.15 and declines to about 1.02; the red “SepLLM (n=128)” line begins near about 1.10 and declines to about 1.01; the purple “SepLLM (n=64, H)” line starts around about 1.12 and decreases to about 1.01; and the brown “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” line starts around about 1.08 and decreases to about 1.00–1.01, with all non-baseline lines showing a downward trend as FLOPs increase.
